analysis: Remaining raw and upper-consumer contract gaps after proposed Entity.roleList and Entity.applicationId additions
assessment_mode: Read-only source inspection. Proposed additions assessed separately from current pre-edit source. No capture probe, API call, application edit or test execution.

observed_source_state.limit: Parent may apply requested BFF changes after this snapshot. Rebind changed hashes before treating this evidence as the final implementation.

findings.class: semantic contract difference; unavoidable without explicit policy
findings.claim: A CES role list cannot preserve the old single-role meaning automatically.
findings.raw_api: roleList is additive. Legacy roleName and roleId remain unset for aggregate CES entities unless a separate projection is defined. A list does not identify one canonical scalar role.
findings.upper_consumers: getUser().role still only reads legacy user.entitlement or X_RATANONE.roleName. Saved filters/views submit a scalar assignee/moduleOwner; PSS_RO restrictions compare one string.
findings.consequence: Adding roleList restores available role names but does not resolve role-dependent behavior. First-role or concatenation projections would invent policy.
findings.next_action: Keep EMS2 scalar role unchanged. Adapt shared role-aware consumers with explicit multi-role rules and retain the original roleList. Do not infer role-to-action attribution from aggregate grants.
findings.limit: No actual new-field execution or role-policy approval assessed.

findings.class: raw identity difference plus fixable shared-adapter gap
findings.claim: New applicationId does not restore old entity identity or permission dispatch.
findings.raw_api: Entity.name remains the CES application name, rather than X_RATANONE. applicationId carries the ITAM ID as a string. These are distinct from the old EMS2 numeric Entity.id.
findings.upper_consumers: hasPermission(code) dispatch still relies on X_RATANONE or entity-name substring matching. getUser().entitlements still keys by entity.name and discards applicationId/roleList.
findings.consequence: The two added fields alone leave previously retained local permission failures intact by source prediction.
findings.next_action: Retain existing boolean permission APIs and feature/action strings. Resolve selected provider and exact application internally, using applicationId where available. Do not alias CES back to X_RATANONE globally.
findings.limit: Prior capture probe was not repeated. No new runtime result claimed.

findings.class: raw token representation difference; fixable shared consumer gap
findings.claim: The entitlement token still encodes name:roleName, not roleList or applicationId.
findings.raw_api: buildEntitlementString produces CES_APPLICATION:null for null legacy roleName. Its map cannot represent multiple role names or same-name distinct application IDs. Adding fields to entities does not change this token.
findings.upper_consumers: Base decodes that token into user.entitlements. Profile dereferences name:roleName; analytics searches X_RATANONE keys.
findings.consequence: Entity fields and legacy token remain separate representations. Token-only consumers do not gain roles or application identity.
findings.next_action: Preserve the legacy token field for existing consumers. Teach shared consumers to use structured entities for CES, or design an additive versioned token claim if token-only consumers need the new metadata. Do not silently replace legacy map keys or manufacture per-role action attribution.
findings.limit: Current Profile token lookup remains aligned with current null key; no current crash inferred from the fields alone.

findings.class: raw source-specific nullability; fixable base type and display gap
findings.claim: Legacy numeric IDs, applicationName, and scalar role fields remain unavailable in CES normalization.
findings.raw_api: Entity.id, roleId, applicationName, roleName and subject/action IDs are not populated by the CES mapper. applicationId should remain a separate string identity.
findings.upper_consumers: Exported base Entity/Subject/Action interfaces require legacy values. Profile labels use applicationName/roleName; keys and ARIA IDs use entity.id.
findings.consequence: Type declarations overstate the CES data contract. Profile can display null role labels and reuse null IDs for multiple CES entities.
findings.next_action: Declare nullable legacy fields and optional/additive roleList/applicationId. Use provider-aware stable profile keys and display the role list. Do not put ITAM IDs into legacy numeric IDs as a compatibility shortcut.
findings.limit: No browser display verification. Duplicate-ID consequence requires multiple CES entities.

findings.class: fixable per-tile adapter and metadata gap
findings.claim: The entity additions do not complete per-tile provider propagation or feature admission semantics.
findings.raw_api: Drawers expose entitlementSource and entity names, but subject still comes from ems2_subject. They do not expose entitlementAppId or entitlementAppFeature in this builder.
findings.upper_consumers: Base validateTile uses legacy subjects; foreign container mount passes only module/tile/parameters/panelId/tabId. Global hasPermission has no tile context.
findings.consequence: Divergent feature names or simultaneous same-feature tiles with different providers cannot be handled safely by the entity fields alone.
findings.next_action: Carry authoritative tile/provider/application bindings through shared internals. Keep existing upper signatures when scope resolves. Do not select provider globally or fall back to another provider after denial. Resolve unavoidable ambiguous no-context call sites explicitly.
findings.limit: Current sample admission previously matched; this is a supported future configuration/design boundary, not a new observed failure.

findings.raw_api: EntityKey consists of name, roleId and roleName. CES entities with equal names and null legacy roles merge subjects. Only the left entity metadata survives.
findings.consequence: If distinct ITAM IDs share an application name, adding applicationId alone cannot preserve separation; role lists from merged rows could also be lost if only mapped without merge handling.
findings.next_action: Preserve explicit application identity in the merge key or record an enforced application-name uniqueness contract. Merge role lists only within the same confirmed application scope.
findings.limit: One application ID in supplied capture. No duplicate-name multi-ID runtime condition established; no application defect confirmed for that capture.

unchanged_or_compatible_boundaries.claim: The login envelope and entity/subject/action arrays can remain structurally compatible through additive fields.
unchanged_or_compatible_boundaries.limit: Strict external JSON consumers are not inventoried; do not claim universal compatibility.

unchanged_or_compatible_boundaries.claim: Existing upper hasPermission(code):boolean signatures and mapped feature/action names need not change in unambiguous scope.
unchanged_or_compatible_boundaries.limit: Shared adapters are still required; same-feature mixed-provider static calls remain a design limit.

unchanged_or_compatible_boundaries.claim: FMO PORTAL ADMIN scalar helper remains a separate legacy consumer.
unchanged_or_compatible_boundaries.limit: No blanket CES admin migration follows from new fields. Preserve EMS2 behavior until explicitly migrated.
